name: Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (BCB) PhD
institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
detailsNote: Official information available; no deadline is printed with a year, so none is confirmed for Fall 2027. The program page lists January 1 for Fall; the Graduate School lists March 1 (priority) and August 1 (final). Confirm which applies. English minimums are the Graduate School's general ones.
summary: Interdisciplinary PhD in bioinformatics and computational biology at UNC Charlotte. The program admits only students whose five-year financial support can be guaranteed; first-year students do two research rotations.

publishedDeadlines.label: Program deadline, Fall admission
publishedDeadlines.note: Printed on the program page and its admissions page without a year. Late applications may be considered if space remains.

publishedDeadlines.note: Graduate School requirements page; no year.

english.toefl: 4.5 for tests taken on or after January 21, 2026; 83 for earlier tests
english.note: Graduate School minimums, for applicants whose native language is not English and who did not earn a U.S. degree. The program page itself lists no English test.

applicationFee.note: $85 for international applicants; $75 for U.S. citizens and permanent residents. The Graduate School gives a limited number of waivers to permanent UNC Charlotte employees, Ronald McNair program participants and U.S. military service members. Confirm whether international applicants qualify.

documents: Unofficial transcripts from all prior higher education institutions
requirements.note: The program page lists excellent GRE scores. The GRE can be waived for applicants with, or completing before enrollment, a U.S. MS degree, or a qualifying U.S. BS degree; a waiver is not an offer of admission.

funding.note: The program page says it only admits students for whom financial support can be guaranteed for five years: a tuition and health insurance award plus a teaching or research assistantship. It does not say whether this covers international students.
